subject.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unsupported OAuth enterprise domain before refresh and model routing

question: Should legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth credentials be restricted to github.com and single-label *.ghe.com tenant roots, with every other persisted origin disabled until reauthentication?
rationale: The patch is mechanically correct, but this choice establishes the permanent allowlist for bearer-token egress and deliberately invalidates existing off-list profiles, so repository automation should not define it alone.

options.title: Confirm the strict allowlist
options.body: Approve github.com and single-label *.ghe.com as the complete supported set and land the current fail-closed behavior after exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Expand the supported contract
options.body: Pause landing and document any additional legitimate Copilot authentication origins before updating the predicate and compatibility tests.

options.title: Retire the legacy OAuth path
options.body: Replace this targeted guard with an explicit doctor migration that removes legacy OAuth profiles in favor of the plugin-owned token profile.

recommendation.title: Confirm the strict allowlist
recommendation.body: Approve github.com and single-label *.ghe.com as the complete supported set and land the current fail-closed behavior after exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Their earlier merged GHE.com Copilot authentication work is the strongest available feature-history signal for confirming the intended host contract.
